title: Late Charge Calculation on the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
A cafe invoice that has stood unpaid beyond its grace days carries a late charge on the contract. On a Workplace Cafe Management Program contract the charge is settled by the clauses below, each quantity being read from the contract's own record.

1. The amount still outstanding is the management fees invoiced on the contract over the twelve months up to the day the charge is raised less the payments received over those same twelve months, and it is never less than nil. Both totals are read from the contract's ledger.
2. The grace days allowed are the late charge grace days printed against the service model.
3. The days overdue run from the day after the management fee invoice most recently posted up to and including the day the charge is raised.
4. The late charge rate is the monthly late charge percentage printed against the service model.
5. The months charged are the days overdue less the grace days allowed, divided by thirty and rounded down to a whole month, and never less than nil.
6. The late charge is the amount still outstanding taken at the late charge rate, rounded to the nearest cent, charged for each month charged, and held to the late charge ceiling printed against the service model.
7. The late charge is recorded against the billing period in which it is raised.

Worked through on hypothetical figures: a contract whose printed late charge grace days stand at 6 calendar days, whose printed monthly late charge percentage stands at 1.1 per cent and whose printed late charge ceiling stands at 3000.00 USD; management fees invoiced of 71456.78 USD and payments received of 48000.00 USD over the twelve months up to the day the charge is raised, so the amount still outstanding is 23456.78 USD; the management fee invoice most recently posted on 2026-02-18 and the charge raised on 2026-06-30, so the days overdue run from 2026-02-19 up to and including 2026-06-30, which is 132 calendar days. The days overdue less the grace days allowed give 126 days; divided by thirty that is 4.2, rounded down to 4 whole months, so the months charged are 4. The amount still outstanding taken at 1.1 per cent is 258.024580 USD, rounded to the nearest cent 258.02 USD, charged for each of the 4 months charged, which is 1032.08 USD; that figure is below the ceiling of 3000.00 USD, so the late charge is 1032.08 USD, recorded against the billing period 2026-06.

Two boundaries on the same hypothetical contract. Where the months charged come to 14, the charge before the ceiling is 3612.28 USD, above the ceiling of 3000.00 USD, so the late charge is held at 3000.00 USD. Where the days overdue are 4 calendar days against grace days allowed of 6 calendar days, the days overdue less the grace days allowed would fall below nil and the months charged are nil, so the late charge is 0.00 USD.
